precepts.text: Walk before me, and be thou perfect: meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says walked with God, it doesn't mean they went on long walks and talks on the beach; it means walked in his ways.
precepts.point: The earth also was corrupt before God: because the sons of God started to mingle with the daughters of men, Cain's children. Cain gained dominion on the earth. And the earth was filled with violence: just like Cain was violent. Is the earth full of violence today? Yes. The end of all flesh is come before me; behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

precepts.text: Abraham was ninety-nine and Ishmael thirteen when circumcised: not the eighth day and no sacrifice, so not after the manner of Moses.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” “And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.”

Abraham was not circumcised on the eighth day after he was born; he was ninety-nine. Ishmael was thirteen. There was no eighth day, no days of purifying and no sacrifice. That is circumcision of the fathers, not circumcision after the manner of Moses.

The Pharisees wanted circumcision and sacrifice together, after the manner of Moses, because sacrificing was their bread and butter. As more people followed Christ, more of them stopped sacrificing, and if the people stop sacrificing, the Pharisees cannot eat. So they went into the churches saying you have to be circumcised to be saved. That is not what the Bible, Christ or the apostles taught. They were trying to put back on the people the yoke that could not be borne, the same one Peter asked about: “why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?”

precepts.text: A perfect heart is one that walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments; that is the meaning of be thou perfect.
precepts.point: Perfect according to the scriptures means to walk in His statutes and keep His commandments; that is how Israel perfects itself.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
What does “be thou perfect” mean? The scriptures define it: “Let your heart therefore be perfect with the Lord our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.” A perfect heart is one that walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments. That is how Israel perfects itself.

Abram was ninety and nine years old when he was commanded to walk before the Most High and be perfect. There is no age excuse. And Christ said nothing new in Matthew 5:48; the command to be perfect was given thousands of years before, right here to Abram, and it has always meant keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: The same covenant words passed to Jacob, named Israel: nations and kings out of his loins.
precepts.point: The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
When the Most High began dealing with Abram on a covenant level, his name was changed: Abram became Abraham, “a father of many nations”, and “kings shall come out of thee.” The same thing happened down the seed line. “Thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name.” And God said to him, “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins.”

Same covenant words: the name changed, exceeding fruitful, nations, kings. Father of many nations does not mean everybody is spiritually a child of Abraham. The promise was passed down the seed line to Jacob, and the nations and kings come out of Israel’s loins.

precepts.text: The blessing of all men and the covenant rested on the head of Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
“Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like unto him; Who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him: he established the covenant in his flesh; and when he was proved, he was found faithful.” Therefore the Lord assured him by an oath “that he would bless the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the stars.”

Then it shows where the promise went. “With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant, And made it rest upon the head of Jacob.” He gave Jacob an heritage and divided his portions: “among the twelve tribes did he part them.”

So the father of many nations is not everybody. The blessing of all men and the covenant rest on the head of Jacob and are divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.

precepts.text: Israel is the servant, Jacob the chosen, the seed of Abraham; Israel is the nation that carries the seed of Abraham.
precepts.point: The covenant is with Abraham's seed after him, and seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor. The Most High promised to be a God to Abraham and to his seed after him.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
The covenant is “between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant.” Seed is literal offspring, not a spiritual metaphor, and Isaiah names that seed: “But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.”

Israel is the servant, Jacob the chosen, the seed of Abraham. Israel is the nation that carries the seed of Abraham, and the Most High promised “to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.” That is the God of Israel.

precepts.text: Circumcision was a seal of the righteousness of the faith Abraham had yet being uncircumcised.
precepts.point: It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
Circumcision is “a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.” Paul explains what it sealed: Abraham “received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised.”

He believed and obeyed first, and then circumcision sealed it. That is the order. Likewise a brother can come into the truth, get built up in the faith, and then go through with the process. But it still has to be done: the token of the covenant is in the flesh, and “the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.”

precepts.text: Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision was implemented; faith and obedience came first.
precepts.point: It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
Two chapters before circumcision was implemented, “he believed in the Lord; and he counted it to him for righteousness.” Abraham was counted righteous before he was circumcised. Faith and obedience came first; circumcision came after, as the seal of the righteousness of the faith he already had.

That is why a brother coming into the truth gets built up in the faith first and then goes through with the process. It does not make circumcision optional: “Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” It just shows the order in which Abraham walked it.

precepts.text: Be mindful always of His covenant, confirmed to Jacob for a law; the covenant carries terms.
precepts.point: It still has to be done. A covenant is a contract with terms; the covenant was confirmed to Jacob for a law, and circumcision is one of the laws within the covenant.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
A covenant is a contract with terms. “Be ye mindful always of his covenant; the word which he commanded to a thousand generations; Even of the covenant which he made with Abraham, and of his oath unto Isaac; And hath confirmed the same to Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant.”

The covenant made with Abraham was confirmed to Jacob for a law. Laws are the terms of the covenant, and circumcision is one of the laws within it: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep.” It was commanded to a thousand generations and it is an everlasting covenant in the flesh, so it still has to be done.

precepts.text: In Isaac shall thy seed be called; the children of the flesh are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.
precepts.point: Not all who are of Abraham's seed are the children; in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai's plan, with no word from God ordaining it; the children of the promise are counted for the seed.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
Ishmael received a blessing: fruitful, multiplied exceedingly, “twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.” But the word to Abraham was kings shall come out of thee, and the covenant goes to one son: “my covenant will I establish with Isaac.”

Paul explains it: “Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called.” Ishmael was born of the flesh, of Sarai’s plan, with no word from God ordaining it. “They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.”

And the word of promise is the very word spoken here: “At this time will I come, and Sara shall have a son.” Isaac, whom Sarah would bear at the set time in the next year, is the child of the promise, and the covenant is with him.

precepts.text: Every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, for an everlasting covenant; the uncircumcised man child shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.
precepts.point: This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai. Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham for every man child in his generations, on the eighth day, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people: he hath broken my covenant. That is why Moses was worthy of death.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
The Lord met Moses in the inn and “sought to kill him” because Moses had not circumcised his son. This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai.

Circumcision was the covenant given to Abraham: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” “And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations”, and “my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.”

“And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.” That is why Moses was worthy of death, and why Zipporah had to take a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son herself.

precepts.text: Abraham was ninety years old and nine when he was circumcised; the covenant is kept at any age.
precepts.point: The Egyptians did not practice circumcision; they were a nation of uncleanness, and the covenant was between the Lord and Israel: after the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.” He took Ishmael and every male in his house “and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.”

The covenant is kept at any age. A son of Israel must be circumcised on the eighth day; and a man that comes to the truth grown must still be circumcised, even at forty, fifty or sixty years, as Abraham himself was circumcised at ninety and nine. The covenant that nearly cost Moses his life still stands.

precepts.text: Every man child eight days old shall be circumcised, an everlasting covenant in the flesh; the uncircumcised is cut off.
precepts.point: That did not change. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John the Baptist, and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
“in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.” The law behind it is the covenant given to Abraham: “Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.”

The day is set there too: “he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations.” And it is not for a season: “my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.”

The penalty is plain: “the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.” That is why brothers coming into the truth must be circumcised.

precepts.text: The covenant with Abraham and his seed: every man child among you shall be circumcised, he that is eight days old, including the servant bought with money.
precepts.point: When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
The Lord tells Joshua to “circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.” Circumcision is the covenant the Most High instituted with our forefather Abraham: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.” It is “a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.” Every man child circumcised at eight days old, and the servant “born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger” circumcised likewise and keeping the laws as well.

The eighth day is the wisdom of the Most High for the body: before then a baby's blood has not begun to coagulate as it needs to, and the child could bleed out; by the eighth day he is strong enough to withstand the process and heal.

There are physical benefits to the law: when the foreskin remains, moisture gets trapped and creates an environment for bacteria, raising the risk of infection and urinary tract infections, and being circumcised even reduces a wife's risk of cervical cancer. This is the Most High as a Father giving his children counsel on how to live and stay clear of disease. The children of Israel in Joshua's day had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them.

precepts.text: Abraham circumcised every male of his house in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him; faith shown by doing.
precepts.point: When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
When Abraham received the commandment he performed it: “And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.” He himself was ninety years old and nine.

The selfsame day: he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed, faith shown by doing. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision, the way Abraham did.

precepts.text: Every man child was to be circumcised, and it was a token of the covenant between the Most High and Abraham's seed.
precepts.point: To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
When Peter came up to Jerusalem, “they that were of the circumcision contended with him, Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” The complaint was about Peter dealing with the Gentiles, meaning the northern kingdom. There had been contention between the northern and southern kingdom ever since the split under Solomon.

To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: “This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised. And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.”

Circumcision was the token, the sign, of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations of his seed.

precepts.text: The uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised shall be cut off; he hath broken my covenant.
precepts.point: To understand circumcision and uncircumcision you have to go to the origin: circumcision was the token, the sign, the seal of the covenant the Most High made with Abraham, a visible confirmation carried through all the generations.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.”

To leave the seal off was to break the covenant and be cut off from his people. That is why the circumcision took it so hard that Peter “wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.”
